caption: How hi q works. You ask in plain words. hi gathers a short, redacted description of where you are, such as the system, the folder, the git state, and recent commands, and sends it with the question to the model you chose: your team's hi server, Claude Code, OpenRouter, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or the Anthropic API. The model may look first with read-only tools that hi runs itself. It answers with one command, which hi shows with its risk; nothing runs until you press Enter.
via: hi q "move the md files into notes"

items.title: hi q --context
items.does: System, shell, folder names, git state, recent commands; keys and secrets removed, no file contents.

items.title: list · read · help · which · run
items.does: hi runs them itself; `run` takes only read-only commands, for 10 seconds at most.

items.title: mkdir -p notes && mv -- *.md notes/
items.does: Shown with what it changes. Enter runs it, `e` edits, `c` copies, `?` explains, Esc cancels.

after.via: the question and context go to

items.title: hi q --status
items.does: Your team's hi server, Claude Code, OpenRouter, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or the Anthropic API, chosen with `hi q --setup`.

key.text: Where the command will run, so the answer fits it.
A short description of where you are; `--no-context` sends only the question.
The model asks, hi looks: nothing it does from here changes anything.

Wherever you chose, often your team's server, with no key on your machine.
